# Expense Tracker (Android)

A simple expense tracker: add expenses (amount, category, optional note), see the running total, delete entries.

**Stack:** Kotlin · Jetpack Compose (Material 3) · Room · ViewModel + Flow · Gradle (Kotlin DSL)

## Structure

```
app/src/main/java/com/example/expensetracker/
├── MainActivity.kt        # Compose UI: list, total, add dialog
├── ExpenseViewModel.kt    # State + add/delete logic, amount parsing
└── data/
    ├── Expense.kt         # Room entity (amount stored in cents)
    ├── ExpenseDao.kt      # Queries
    └── AppDatabase.kt     # Room database singleton
```

## Build & run

1. Open the `expense-tracker-android` folder in Android Studio (Ladybug / 2024.2 or newer).
2. Let Gradle sync. Android Studio will generate the Gradle wrapper jar if missing;
   otherwise run `gradle wrapper --gradle-version 8.9` once from a machine with Gradle installed.
3. Run on a device/emulator with API 24+.

Requirements: JDK 17, Android SDK 35.

content.text:
The Android project is in `expense-tracker-android/`. I did not build or compile it, as you asked.

**Features:** add an expense (amount, category, optional note), see the running total, delete entries. Amounts are stored in cents, and a comma or dot is accepted as the decimal separator.

**Stack:** Kotlin, Jetpack Compose (Material 3), Room, ViewModel with Flow, Gradle Kotlin DSL. The minimum SDK is 24 and the target SDK is 35.

**Files:**
- `settings.gradle.kts`, `build.gradle.kts`, `gradle.properties`, `.gitignore`, `README.md`
- `gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties` (Gradle 8.9)
- `app/build.gradle.kts`, `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`, `app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml`
- `app/src/main/java/com/example/expensetracker/MainActivity.kt`: Compose UI, list, total, add dialog
- `app/src/main/java/com/example/expensetracker/ExpenseViewModel.kt`: add/delete logic and amount parsing
- `app/src/main/java/com/example/expensetracker/data/`: `Expense.kt`, `ExpenseDao.kt`, `AppDatabase.kt`

**Before the first build:**
- The Gradle wrapper jar is not included. Open the folder in Android Studio and let it sync, or run `gradle wrapper --gradle-version 8.9` once.
- The dependency versions (AGP 8.5.2, Kotlin 2.0.21, Compose BOM 2024.09.00, Room 2.6.1) are from memory and have not been checked against a build. If sync fails on a version, that is the first place to look.
should add a view to manage the types of expenses and when adding an expense should tag it with one or more types.

I'll add a many-to-many link between expenses and types. This needs a Room schema change (version 2) with a migration that keeps existing data. The old free-text category field is replaced by type tags, and existing categories become types.

package com.example.expensetracker.data

import androidx.room.Entity
import androidx.room.ForeignKey
import androidx.room.Index

/** Many-to-many link: an expense can carry several types, and a type can be on many expenses. */
@Entity(
    tableName = "expense_type_cross_ref",
    primaryKeys = ["expenseId", "typeId"],
    foreignKeys = [
        ForeignKey(
            entity = Expense::class,
            parentColumns = ["id"],
            childColumns = ["expenseId"],
            onDelete = ForeignKey.CASCADE
        ),
        ForeignKey(
            entity = ExpenseType::class,
            parentColumns = ["id"],
            childColumns = ["typeId"],
            onDelete = ForeignKey.CASCADE
        )
    ],
    indices = [Index(value = ["typeId"])]
)
data class ExpenseTypeCrossRef(
    val expenseId: Long,
    val typeId: Long
)

package com.example.expensetracker.data

import androidx.room.migration.Migration
import androidx.sqlite.db.SupportSQLiteDatabase

/**
 * v1 -> v2: the free-text `category` column becomes a set of types.
 * Each distinct old category is turned into an expense_type and linked to its expense.
 */
val MIGRATION_1_2 = object : Migration(1, 2) {
    override fun migrate(db: SupportSQLiteDatabase) {
        db.execSQL(
            "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `expense_types` " +
                "(`id` INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT NOT NULL, `name` TEXT NOT NULL)"
        )
        db.execSQL(
            "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS `index_expense_types_name` " +
                "ON `expense_types` (`name`)"
        )

        // Capture old categories before the expenses table is rebuilt.
        db.execSQL(
            "CREATE TEMP TABLE `tmp_old_tags` AS " +
                "SELECT id AS expenseId, TRIM(category) AS name FROM expenses WHERE TRIM(category) <> ''"
        )
        db.execSQL("INSERT OR IGNORE INTO expense_types (name) SELECT DISTINCT name FROM tmp_old_tags")

        // Rebuild expenses without the category column (DROP COLUMN is not available on all API 24+ devices).
        db.execSQL(
            "CREATE TABLE `expenses_new` (`id` INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT NOT NULL, " +
                "`amountCents` INTEGER NOT NULL, `note` TEXT NOT NULL, `dateMillis` INTEGER NOT NULL)"
        )
        db.execSQL(
            "INSERT INTO expenses_new (id, amountCents, note, dateMillis) " +
                "SELECT id, amountCents, note, dateMillis FROM expenses"
        )
        db.execSQL("DROP TABLE expenses")
        db.execSQL("ALTER TABLE expenses_new RENAME TO expenses")

        db.execSQL(
            "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `expense_type_cross_ref` (" +
                "`expenseId` INTEGER NOT NULL, `typeId` INTEGER NOT NULL, " +
                "PRIMARY KEY(`expenseId`, `typeId`), " +
                "FOREIGN KEY(`expenseId`) REFERENCES `expenses`(`id`) ON UPDATE NO ACTION ON DELETE CASCADE, " +
                "FOREIGN KEY(`typeId`) REFERENCES `expense_types`(`id`) ON UPDATE NO ACTION ON DELETE CASCADE)"
        )
        db.execSQL(
            "CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS `index_expense_type_cross_ref_typeId` " +
                "ON `expense_type_cross_ref` (`typeId`)"
        )
        db.execSQL(
            "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO expense_type_cross_ref (expenseId, typeId) " +
                "SELECT t.expenseId, et.id FROM tmp_old_tags t JOIN expense_types et ON et.name = t.name"
        )
        db.execSQL("DROP TABLE tmp_old_tags")
    }
}

# Expense Tracker (Android)

Track expenses with an amount, optional note, and one or more **types** (tags such as "Food" or "Travel").
Types are managed in a separate view (Types → add / rename / delete). Running total is shown on the main screen.

**Stack:** Kotlin · Jetpack Compose (Material 3) · Room (schema v2) · ViewModel + Flow · Gradle (Kotlin DSL)

## Structure

```
app/src/main/java/com/example/expensetracker/
├── MainActivity.kt        # Compose UI: expenses screen, add dialog, types screen
├── ExpenseViewModel.kt    # State + validation + add/delete logic, amount parsing
└── data/
    ├── Expense.kt             # Expense entity (amount in cents)
    ├── ExpenseType.kt         # Type entity (unique name)
    ├── ExpenseTypeCrossRef.kt # Many-to-many link expense <-> type
    ├── ExpenseWithTypes.kt    # Relation: expense + its types
    ├── ExpenseDao.kt
    ├── ExpenseTypeDao.kt
    ├── Migrations.kt          # v1 -> v2: old category text becomes types
    └── AppDatabase.kt
```

## Build & run

1. Open the `expense-tracker-android` folder in Android Studio (Ladybug / 2024.2 or newer).
2. Let Gradle sync. Android Studio will generate the Gradle wrapper jar if missing;
   otherwise run `gradle wrapper --gradle-version 8.9` once from a machine with Gradle installed.
3. Run on a device/emulator with API 24+.

Requirements: JDK 17, Android SDK 35.

## Notes

- Existing v1 data is migrated: each distinct old category becomes a type and is linked to its expense.
- Deleting a type removes it from all expenses (the expenses themselves are kept).
- The migration and Room schema have not been compiled or run; verify on first launch with an existing v1 database.

content.text:
I added a Types management view and multi-type tagging to the expense form. Nothing has been compiled or run.

**What changed** (in `expense-tracker-android/`):
- **Types view:** opened from the "Types" button in the top bar of the expenses screen. It lets you add a type, rename it by tapping it, and delete it with the trash icon. Names are unique, ignoring case.
- **Add expense:** the free-text category field is replaced by selectable type chips. You can pick one or more. Saving requires at least one type and an amount above 0. If no types exist yet, the dialog tells you to create some first.
- **Expense list:** each row shows its types, comma-separated.
- **Data model:** a many-to-many link between expenses and types (`ExpenseType`, `ExpenseTypeCrossRef`, `ExpenseWithTypes`). The database is now version 2.

**Decisions to check:**
- **Existing data is migrated.** Each distinct old category becomes a type and is linked to its expense. The migration rebuilds the `expenses` table because `DROP COLUMN` isn't safe on all API 24+ devices.
- **Deleting a type removes it from every expense** but keeps the expenses. The Types screen says so. There is no confirmation dialog.
- **At least one type is required** per expense. Say if you want it optional.

**Not verified:** the Room schema, the migration SQL, and the Compose code have not been compiled or run. The migration is the riskiest part. Test it by installing the v1 build, adding expenses, then upgrading to this version.

content.text:
I removed the migration. `Migrations.kt` is deleted, and the database now uses `fallbackToDestructiveMigration()` in `AppDatabase.kt`.

The consequence: anyone who installed the first (v1) build will have their existing expenses dropped when they upgrade to this version. The README says so. Fresh installs are unaffected.
